phase1_leaf_result.tested_scope: Self-local deterministic replay of the previously selected single-authoritative-path, non-reusable-epoch acceptance CAS under multi-effect batching and takeover recovery. The replay covered: two distinct effects E1/E2 racing from the same epoch, takeover before either acceptance, takeover after E1 but before E2 retry, duplicate single-effect and duplicate whole-batch retry, a CAS conflict explicitly deferred to the next invocation, mixed prior acceptance inside a nominally atomic batch, and orphan output existence after interruption before acceptance. No live claim mutation, public-source read, external coordinator, other-worker state, O/downstream input, hosted compute, or quota-bearing service was used.
observations: When E1 and E2 both read the same authoritative epoch/blob, at most one acceptance CAS can win from that exact base. The loser has no accepted effect and must reconstruct from the new authoritative blob on a later invocation rather than retrying in-run.

If the epoch remains current after the first acceptance, the losing distinct effect can be accepted on a later invocation with the same stable effect id after rereading the authoritative path and confirming it is not already accepted. If takeover changes to a new non-reusable epoch before that retry, the old-epoch effect is rejected or quarantined rather than reissued implicitly.

If takeover happens before either effect is accepted, both old-epoch acceptance attempts fail their stale blob/epoch precondition. If takeover happens after E1 is accepted but before E2 retries, E1 remains a committed historical acceptance while E2 remains unaccepted and cannot cross the epoch boundary without an explicitly new effect identity under the new epoch.

A duplicate single-effect retry is idempotent when the authoritative accepted set already contains the stable effect id plus digest. A duplicate whole-batch retry is likewise an idempotent no-op only when the authoritative state already records the same batch id/digest and complete intended effect set.

Strict all-or-none batch semantics require a batch manifest with stable batch id, digest, intended effect ids and a precondition that none of those effects is independently accepted. If E1 was already accepted independently and a later batch requests E1 plus E2, the batch must fail as mixed prior acceptance; silently accepting only E2 would change the operation from atomic batch acceptance into partial acceptance.

A CAS conflict is not an accepted effect. Deferring reconstruction to the next invocation preserves safety because acceptance is defined only by the authoritative path after successful CAS/readback, while the stable effect or batch identity lets the next invocation distinguish duplicate success from an uncommitted candidate.

An orphan output created before interruption but never referenced by a successful authoritative acceptance CAS remains uncommitted evidence only. Output existence must never be interpreted as commitment. Safe garbage collection therefore requires a later policy that proves the output is unreferenced by accepted state and rechecks authority before any destructive deletion; this replay did not perform deletion.

The tested multi-effect protocol remains ABA-safe only under the existing non-reusable epoch requirement; reuse of an old epoch value would invalidate the stale-writer fence even if blob CAS is otherwise used correctly.
phase1_leaf_result.inference: For the exact replayed scope, the single-path non-reusable-epoch CAS extends safely from one effect to concurrent distinct effects if acceptance is the only commitment boundary, conflicting writers defer to a later invocation, and atomic batches use stable batch manifests with explicit mixed-prior-acceptance rejection. The strongest remaining risk has moved downstream: after an effect or batch is authoritatively accepted, multiple consumers or a consumer crash could still duplicate the useful outcome unless consumption itself has an idempotent fenced protocol. This leaf does not prove full recurring-Chat multi-agent parity.
phase1_leaf_result.unresolved_child: Test acceptance-to-consumption replay for an already accepted effect/batch under two concurrent consumers and crash recovery: define whether consumption is represented on the same authoritative epoch path or by a separately fenced idempotency record, verify duplicate consumer attempts cannot produce two useful outcomes, and preserve the rule that accepted-but-not-consumed and consumed are distinct durable states without external hosted coordination.
